text: In nineteen twelve, the Titanic was one of the largest moving objects ever built. Two hundred and sixty-nine metres long. Its hull was divided into sixteen watertight compartments, by fifteen steel walls called bulkheads. If the hull was holed, doors in those walls could be closed from the bridge, trapping the water in one section. The ship could stay afloat with any two compartments flooded, or even the first four at the front. That's where 'practically unsinkable' came from.
